premise: A sealed women's ward isolation cell (two cots, shared head, a reinforced door, and a high observation aperture) makes first contact intimate before the larger system commits: whoever already reads the room sets tempo for cohabitation, and noise from the corridor is a reminder that power can re-enter at any moment. Intake is lived here; informal hierarchy and fear of the next move (rounds, shower blocks, the mess) shape what gets said and what is deferred until staff, a ward peer enforcer, or a credentialed officer steps into view.
